Direct support-function evaluation gives |x_i-x_j|<=(w_i+w_j)/2, each supporting an actual facet; there are n(n-1) oriented facets. Central symmetry guarantees a globally optimal origin-centered inball with radius r=min_{i<j}(w_i+w_j)/(2sqrt2). Erosion by the Euclidean ball gives all optimal centers as |z_i-z_j|<=(w_i+w_j-s)/2. For every minimum-sum pair an edge of G_s, equality forces z_i=z_j; for every nonedge the inequality is strictly slack at z=0 in the component-constant subspace, proving affdim c(G_s)-1. A min-weight multiplicity k>=2 gives clique K_k and n-k free components; unique min with q second-minimizers gives star K_{1,q} and n-q-1; unique center iff all tied or unique lightest with all others equally second. The projected-box corner has squared norm [Σw_i²−(Σeps_i w_i)²/n]/4. Mixed-sign patterns expose distinct zonotope vertices, and every all-same-sign pattern can be improved in absolute discrepancy by one flip; maximizing the convex norm over the corners gives exactly the signed-discrepancy minimizers as outer contacts, with unique circumcenter by antipodal symmetry. PARTITION equivalence is precisely weak NP-completeness under positive integral weights. Independently tested 5 weight patterns (ties and strictly increasing cases), all corner facet inequalities, signed discrepancy radius, predicted G_s center affine dimensions and facet contacts. These finite examples do not prove the all-n arbitrary-real result.
